notes:
VERDICT: BLOCKED. create_test_plan_by_integer_id could not create a test plan in 3/3 attempts against tm preprod, project PR-2005 (379335744). Two attempts sent a structurally-valid flat body (confirmed valid by invokeCapability's own accepted-keys error message) and both got a reproducible, undeclared HTTP 500 {status:500, error:'Internal Server Error'} — not one of the 6 documented error shapes. This is a genuine live defect on this route, not a probe-shape mistake: the setup-step re-list of the project (list_test_plans_by_integer_id, count.active=29, matching the pool's stated baseline) confirms no plan was created and none leaked — the 500s are real failures, not success-with-bad-envelope.

JSON_PATH WRAPPER TRAP CONFIRMED (attempt 2): describeCapability's json_path values and its own prose guidance both explicitly instruct wrapping the body under a `test_plan` key ('Every field goes inside a `test_plan` object. A flat body is rejected before any field is read.'). Live behaviour is the opposite: the wrapped body is rejected client-side with 'unknown body: test_plan', and the flat body is the one invokeCapability accepts (it just then 500s server-side). An agent that followed the documented guidance verbatim on its first call would get a client-side rejection; an agent that then 'fixed' it by flattening would hit a 500 with no plan created — this route is unusable via the documented contract as written.

SPECIFIC INTEREST — run-plan linkage at creation: UNVERIFIED, could not be determined. Both flat-body attempts included test_runs:[17575382] (TR-9062's integer uuid, per the contract's own stated form: 'run INTEGER ids (a run's uuid, not its TR-NNN id)'). The body-name validator in attempt 2 confirms `test_runs` IS a recognised field name for this route (it appears in the exhaustive 'accepted:' list), so the integer-uuid form was at minimum accepted at the field-name level — but since every attempt 500'd before any create response came back, it was never possible to confirm (a) whether the integer id form is actually honoured server-side, (b) whether a prefixed 'TR-9062' string would also be accepted, or (c) whether a successful create would reflect the link (test_runs_count / test_plan.test_runs). Given the 3-attempt cap was reached, this could not be isolated further (e.g. retrying without test_runs to see if it is specifically the linkage code path causing the 500, vs. some other server bug). This remains open and worth a dedicated follow-up probe with a fresh attempt budget: if create_test_plan_by_integer_id 500s even with test_runs omitted entirely, the defect is unrelated to run-linking; if it succeeds without test_runs, that would strongly implicate the run-attach code path as the crash source, corroborating the already-known read-side breakage (list_test_runs_by_integer_id never reporting test_plans despite metadata.test_plan_error='PLAN_LINKED' on TR-9061).

ENTITLEMENT-GATE PATTERN: NOT OBSERVED here. All three failures were real 500s (or a client-side shape rejection), never a 200 {success:false} — so this capability does not exhibit the '200-wearing-a-refusal' pattern seen elsewhere; the defect here is a distinct one (undeclared 500 envelope on structurally-valid input).
